acme-integration: Hey team — running into a weird issue with the batch /rerank endpoint. We send a multi-query batch (N=6 queries) with variable candidate list lengths and some queries return scores, but they appear shifted — i.e. scores from query i+1 are attached to query i. Example payload (simplified):
```json
{
  "model": "rerank-v2",
  "queries": [
    {"id": "q1", "candidates": ["A","B"]},
    {"id": "q2", "candidates": ["C"]},
    {"id": "q3", "candidates": []},
    {"id": "q4", "candidates": ["D","E","F"]}
  ]
}
```
We get HTTP 200 but the scores array length is equal to total candidates (6) and they are in one flat list — but mapping back to queries uses the wrong offsets. Any guidance?

lexi (support): Thanks for the report — can you paste the exact curl you used and the response body (or at least the scores section)? Also confirm API version and region. Do you see any 4xx/5xx? Is there an x-request-id in the response headers?

acme-integration: Sure — curl below, response snippet. We do see x-request-id: rq_01G7XXX. No 4xx/5xx, just incorrect mapping.
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank/batch \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d @payload.json
```
Response (trimmed):
```json
{
  "request_id": "rq_01G7XXX",
  "scores": [0.92, 0.33, 0.78, 0.12, 0.55, 0.41],
  "candidates_total": 6
}
```
Expected mapping: q1->(0.92,0.33), q2->(0.78), q3->(), q4->(0.12,0.55,0.41) — but actual mapping in our client is q1->(0.92), q2->(0.33,0.78), q3->(0.12), q4->(0.55,0.41) (looks like a one-off shift).

devon (runtime): @lexi looking — this smells like the offsets calculation in the batch flattening logic. We had a recent change to support empty candidate lists that touched the offsets accumulator. Can you confirm if any queries had "candidates": [] (you showed q3 empty) and whether you included an explicit "per_query_counts" or used implicit counting?

acme-integration: We did not include per_query_counts. We assumed server would infer counts from nested arrays (like previous versions). Quick note: one of our older clients flattens candidates into a single array and sends a separate counts array; new client sends nested arrays. Not sure if that matters.

samir (eng): For context — there was a similar bug tracked internally where empty candidate lists were skipped by the flatten routine which caused offsets to slide left. Stack trace we saw locally while reproing: IndexError when mapping scores -> candidate index, then fallback to returning flat scores with incorrect grouping. Repro command we used:
```bash
python tests/repro_batch_rerank.py --cases multi_empty --model rerank-v2 --host canary.redwood.ai
```
I can repro locally against canary.

ops-bot: [automated log] 1799802520 ERROR batch_rerank_v2: mapping_offsets: computed_offsets=[0,2,3,3,6], scores_len=6, mismatch -> IndexError: list index out of range (stack=runtime/batch/mapper.py:87)

lexi (support): @acme-integration thanks — two immediate asks: 1) can you try the workaround of splitting the batch into individual /rerank calls for queries that have empty candidate lists or varying lengths? That will confirm it's offsets-related. 2) please share the full response headers for rq_01G7XXX so we can correlate logs (x-request-id, host, timestamp).

acme-integration: Tried splitting into individual calls — that fixes the mapping (scores line up) but doubles overall latency (we have ~150ms per small call vs. ~200ms for whole batch previously). Headers for rq_01G7XXX: x-request-id: rq_01G7XXX, server: redwood/2.3.1, date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 15:27:03 GMT.

devon (runtime): We have a patch ready that reintroduces the empty-list sentinel into the offsets accumulator. Pushed to canary at 1799815000, rolling test now. If canary looks good we'll hotfix prod. Workaround confirmed as expected. ETA to prod if tests pass: ~2 hours. Will follow up with release note and the PR link.

samir (eng): Also note: clients that send flattened candidates + counts should work — but there's a mismatch if server expects nested arrays. We'll add defensive validation to return 400 when counts and nested arrays disagree. That will prevent silent mis-mapping in future.

acme-integration: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Can we get a staging patch earlier? We have traffic peaks and would rather not switch to per-request calls. Also will need a billing credit for the incorrect outputs that affected our A/B results.

lexi (support): Opening escalation INC-4521 and billing review. @devon / @samir marking high priority. acme-integration: I'll DM for the billing details and note outage impact. Ops will post a postmortem link after the fix.

devon (runtime): Canary tests look green at 1799816005. Planning prod rollout at 1799818800 (in ~2 hrs). We'll tag the release as hotfix/rerank-offset-179981 and include migration notes.

acme-integration: Thanks all — letting our SREs know and we'll monitor. Will report back if we still see misalignments after the rollout. :pray:

lexi (support): Closing loop for now, keeping thread open until prod roll and customer confirms. If you need higher-urgency, react with :rotating_light: and we'll expedite.
